decision_conditions: The development to which this permission relates must be begun not later than the expiration of three years beginning with the date of the decision notice. Reason: To comply with the provisions of S.51 of the Planning & Compulsory Purchase Act 2004.

The development hereby permitted shall be carried out in accordance with the following approved plans:Location Plan Dated 29.06.2026Existing and Proposed Block Plan EP001 Dated 18.05.2026Existing Floor Plans E001 Dated 11.05.2026Existing Front and Rear Elevations E002 Dated 11.05.2026Existing Side Elevations E003 Dated 11.05.2026Existing Section E004 Dated 11.05.2026Proposed Floor Plans P001 Dated 01.06.2026Proposed Front and Rear Elevations P002 Dated 01.06.2026Proposed Side Elevations P003 Dated 01.06.2026Proposed Section P004 Dated 01.06.2026Highway Safety Impact FormPlanning Statement Dated June 2026SUDS Pro FormaReason: For the avoidance of doubt and in the interests of proper planning.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied by more than six residents at any one time without first obtaining the approval, in writing, of the Local Planning Authority. Reason: To ensure that the future occupation of the building does not adversely affect neighbouring residential amenity or the character of the immediate area.

No independent cooking or laundry facilities shall be installed in any of the respective bedrooms and the communal kitchen and dining/living rooms shall be retained in perpetuity. Reason: To accord with the stipulations of definition as a House of Multiple Occupation and to safeguard the residential character of the surrounding area.

The development hereby permitted shall not be occupied until waste storage and recycling facilities to satisfy the future number of occupiers on site have been provided within the development, in accordance with the Enfield's Household Recycling and Waste Planning Guidance for New Developments (February 2024). Such facilities to be retained permanently thereafter.Reason: To safeguard the amenity of the occupiers of adjoining premises; protect the general environment; prevent any obstruction to pedestrian movement and to ensure that there are adequate facilities for the storage and recycling of recoverable materials.
The external finishing materials shall match those used in the construction of the existing building and/or areas of hard surfacing. Reason: To ensure a satisfactory appearance.

Prior to first occupation of the HMO hereby approved, details of cycle parking shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. Cycle parking, shall be provided in accordance with the following requirements:o Provision of a minimum of SIX long stay cycle parking spaces;o in an accessible location; the store door must have a minimum opening width of 1.2mo long stay cycle parking spaces secured with a British Standard mortice lock or access fob;o fully enclosed: 4 walls and a roof.o The details shall demonstrate that the cycle parking can be accessed safely and conveniently, without requiring bicycles to be manoeuvred through unsuitable internal living or kitchen areas.Reason: To ensure the provision of accessible, secure, and adequate cycle parking facilities and to safeguard the character and appearance of the area.

Prior to first occupation of the HMO hereby approved, a revised communal kitchen/dining room layout plan shall be submitted to and approved in writing by the Local Planning Authority. The plan shall show that occupiers are not required to pass cooking facilities in order to reach the internal exit from the room. The approved layout, including the additional cooker, shall be implemented prior to first occupation and retained thereafter.Reason: To secure adequate shared kitchen facilities and a safe and satisfactory layout for future occupiers, including an acceptable means of escape from the communal kitchen/dining room.
